newsitem.title: UK: British Steel, exporters up as pound wobbles.
newsitem.headline: British Steel, exporters up as pound wobbles.

text.p: Shares in major UK exporters rose on Friday as the pound wobbled against major currencies in the wake of the landslide election victory by the Labour Party, dealers said.
British Steel Plc rose 3-3/4p to 143 by 0851 GMT, and other engineering stocks also rose with Siebe Plc up 5p at 922-1/2, TI Group Plc up 10p to 543-1/2 and Smiths Industries Plc up 9p at 766-1/2.
BTR Plc was up 1p at 253 and Rolls-Royce Plc was up 2p at 244-1/2.

"It is all on the back of the currency," said one market-maker in engineering stocks. "They have been bombed out on the currency's strength and now they are having a rally on the back of its weakness."
Sterling was off its lows but still down more than two pfennigs and nearly two cents from pre-election result levels.
Currency dealers cited a report in the Times that the new government must create the conditions for an immediate drop in the pound to avoid damage to the economy.

Sterling weakness also proved positive for other overseas earners. Reuters Holdings Plc, for instance -- which warned last month that it expected little or no growth in headline pre-tax profit at the half-year stage because of the strong pound -- was up 17p at 676-1/2.
Reuters also continued to be boosted by positive comment following this week's New York analyst briefings, dealers said.
